stem: Curve X shows 1.0 g granulated zinc reacting with excess hydrochloric acid at 30 °C. Which change gives curve Y?
construction_note_en: Original tests: interpreting a gas-volume-time graph to distinguish reaction rate from final amount of gas, then mapping both features to experimental changes. Correct: D. Curve Y is slower than X and reaches about half the final gas volume. Halving the zinc mass halves the limiting amount of zinc, so the final hydrogen volume is lower; lowering temperature slows particle collisions, so the rate is lower. Distractor types: A is Type B, partly correct on lower temperature but powdered zinc increases surface area and full mass keeps final volume equal to X. B is Type D, lower temperature slows rate but full zinc mass gives the same final volume as X. C is Type A, half mass gives lower final volume but higher temperature increases rate, the opposite of curve Y. Cognitive dimensions: graph interpretation, limiting reagent reasoning, collision theory, variable isolation, proportional reasoning. Item classification: specific knowledge is collision theory and metal-acid hydrogen production; general ability is reading slope and asymptote from a graph and combining two independent variables.
